033/**
034 * Formats a log event using a {@link StringBuilder}. <strong>All formatters should be
035 * thread-safe!</strong>.
036 * <p>
037 * The appender will make sure the {@link StringBuilder} is not shared with multiple
038 * threads so the formatter does not have to synchronize/lock on and should definitely not
039 * do that.
040 * <p>
041 * Because of various invariants the preferred way to compose formatters is to use the
042 * {@linkplain #builder() builder} which will do some optimization like combining static
043 * formatters etc.
044 *
045 * @see #builder()
046 * @see LogFormatter.EventFormatter
047 * @see LogEncoder#of(LogFormatter)
048 * @apiNote This class is sealed. An interface that has the same contract that can be
049 * implemented is {@link EventFormatter}.
050 */
051public sealed interface LogFormatter {
052
053        /**
054         * Formats a log event.
055         * @param output buffer.
056         * @param event log event.
057         * @see EventFormatter
058         */
059        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event);
060
061        /**
062         * See {@link EventFormatter#builder()}.
063         * @return builder.
064         */
065        public static Builder builder() {
066                return new Builder();
067        }
068
069        /**
070         * Create a formatter using event formatter that is a lambda so that
071         * {@code LogFormater.of((o, e) -> ...); } works.
072         * @param e will be returned.
073         * @return passed in formatter.
074         * @apiNote this is for ergonomics because LogFormatter is sealed.
075         */
076        public static EventFormatter of(EventFormatter e) {
077                return e;
078        }
079
080        /**
081         * Ask the formatter if will do anything.
082         * @return true if promises not to write to builder.
083         * @see #noop()
084         */
085        default boolean isNoop() {
086                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE == this;
087        }
088
089        /**
090         * A special formatter that will do nothing. It is a singleton so identity comparison
091         * can be used.
092         * @return a formatter that implements all formatting interfaces but does nothing.
093         */
094        public static NoopFormatter noop() {
095                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE;
096        }
097
098        /**
099         * A special formatter that will append static text.
100         *
101         * @param content static text.
102         */
103        public record StaticFormatter(String content) implements LogFormatter {
104                @Override
105                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
106                        output.append(content);
107                }
108
109                /**
110                 * Creates a new formatter by concat the {@link #content()}. This is mainly used
111                 * by the {@link EventFormatter#builder()} to coalesce multiple static text.
112                 * @param next the text that will follow this formatter.
113                 * @return new formatter.
114                 */
115                public StaticFormatter concat(StaticFormatter next) {
116                        return new StaticFormatter(this.content + next.content);
117                }
118
119                /**
120                 * Coalesce formatters that can be such as {@link StaticFormatter}.
121                 * @param formatters list of formatters in the order of which they will be
122                 * executed.
123                 * @return an array of formatters where static formatters next to each other will
124                 * be coalesced.
125                 */
126                private static LogFormatter[] coalesce(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
127                        var flattened = CompositeFormatter.flatten(formatters);
128                        List<LogFormatter> resolved = new ArrayList<>();
129                        StaticFormatter current = null;
130                        for (var f : flattened) {
131                                if (f.isNoop()) {
132                                }
133                                else if (current == null && f instanceof StaticFormatter sf) {
134                                        current = sf;
135                                }
136                                else if (current != null && f instanceof StaticFormatter sf) {
137                                        current = current.concat(sf);
138                                }
139                                else if (current != null) {
140                                        resolved.add(current);
141                                        resolved.add(f);
142                                        current = null;
143                                }
144                                else {
145                                        resolved.add(f);
146                                }
147                        }
148                        if (current != null) {
149                                resolved.add(current);
150                        }
151                        return resolved.toArray(new LogFormatter[] {});
152                }
153
154                @Override
155                public String toString() {
156                        return "STATIC['" + content + "']";
157                }
158        }
159
160        /**
161         * Controls how a <code>null</code> key value is handled by formatters that print a
162         * <strong>selected</strong> subset of keys (e.g.
163         * {@link Builder#encodedKeyValues(List, KeyValueNullStrategy)}), as opposed to
164         * formatters that print whatever the underlying {@link KeyValues} actually contains
165         * (e.g. {@link Builder#encodedKeyValues()}), which always {@link #KEEP} the
166         * <code>null</code>/empty-string distinction since they have no "selection" step to
167         * apply a strategy to.
168         * <p>
169         * A selected key is treated identically whether it is missing from the
170         * {@link KeyValues} entirely or present but mapped to <code>null</code> -
171         * {@link KeyValues#getValueOrNull(String)} cannot tell those two cases apart, so
172         * neither can this.
173         */
174        @CaseChanging
175        public enum KeyValueNullStrategy {
176
177                /**
178                 * The key is omitted entirely (no key, no <code>=</code>) if its value is
179                 * <code>null</code>.
180                 */
181                SKIP,
182                /**
183                 * A <code>null</code> value is normalized to an empty string, so the key is
184                 * always printed as <code>key=</code> (with nothing after the <code>=</code>)
185                 * regardless of whether the underlying value was <code>null</code> or actually an
186                 * empty string.
187                 */
188                EMPTY,
189                /**
190                 * The <code>null</code>/empty-string distinction is preserved: a
191                 * <code>null</code> value prints just the key with no <code>=</code>, while an
192                 * empty string prints <code>key=</code>. This is the same behavior as
193                 * {@link Builder#encodedKeyValues()} and is the default for
194                 * {@link Builder#encodedKeyValues(List)} - most key values (e.g. MDC) are never
195                 * actually mapped to <code>null</code> in practice, so {@link #SKIP} and
196                 * {@link #KEEP} behave identically until they are.
197                 */
198                KEEP;
199
200        }
201
202        /**
203         * Log formatter builder that is composed of other formatters. The
204         * {@link #add(LogFormatter)} are executed in insertion order. <strong> This builder
205         * is smart and will coalesce and consolidate formatters! </strong> For example if
206         * only formatter is added to the builder it will be returned instead of a new
207         * formatter.
208         */
209        public final static class Builder {
210
211                private List<LogFormatter> formatters = new ArrayList<>();
212
213                private Builder() {
214                }
215
216                /**
217                 * Adds a formatter.
218                 * @param formatter formatter to be added the list of formatters.
219                 * @return this builder.
220                 */
221                public Builder add(LogFormatter formatter) {
222                        formatters.add(formatter);
223                        return this;
224                }
225
226                /**
227                 * Adds an event formatter.
228                 * @param formatter event formatter to be added the list of formatters.
229                 * @return this builder.
230                 */
231                public Builder event(LogFormatter.EventFormatter formatter) {
232                        formatters.add(formatter);
233                        return this;
234                }
235
236                /**
237                 * Append the timestamp in ISO format.
238                 * @return this builder.
239                 */
240                public Builder timeStamp() {
241                        formatters.add(DefaultInstantFormatter.ISO);
242                        return this;
243                }
244
245                /**
246                 * Formatter for {@link LogEvent#timestamp()} derived from standard
247                 * {@link DateTimeFormatter}.
248                 * @param dateTimeFormatter formatter for {@link LogEvent#timestamp()}
249                 * @return this builder.
250                 */
251                public Builder timeStamp(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter) {
252                        formatters.add(TimestampFormatter.of(dateTimeFormatter));
253                        return this;
254                }
255
256                /**
257                 * Adds the default level formatter.
258                 * @return this builder.
259                 * @see LevelFormatter
260                 */
261                public Builder level() {
262                        formatters.add(LogFormatter.LevelFormatter.of());
263                        return this;
264                }
265
266                /**
267                 * Adds the default logger name formatter.
268                 * @return this builder.
269                 */
270                public Builder loggerName() {
271                        formatters.add(DefaultNameFormatter.LOGGER_NAME_FORMATTER);
272                        return this;
273                }
274
275                /**
276                 * Formats the message by calling
277                 * {@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)}.
278                 * @return this builder.
279                 */
280                public Builder message() {
281                        formatters.add(DefaultMessageFormatter.MESSAGE_FORMATTER);
282                        return this;
283                }
284
285                /**
286                 * Appends static text.
287                 * @param content static text.
288                 * @return this builder.
289                 * @see StaticFormatter
290                 */
291                public Builder text(String content) {
292                        formatters.add(new StaticFormatter(content));
293                        return this;
294                }
295
296                /**
297                 * Creates a formatter that will print <strong>ALL</strong> of the key values the
298                 * same way Logback's <code>%X</code>/<code>%mdc</code> does: comma-space
299                 * separated <code>key=value</code> pairs with no surrounding braces (unlike
300                 * Log4j2, which wraps the same pairs in <code>{}</code>), and no percent
301                 * encoding. An empty map renders as an empty string. Keys that are mapped to
302                 * <code>null</code> will only have the key printed and no separating equal sign
303                 * (<code>=</code>), to differentiate empty string and <code>null</code>. For the
304                 * percent-encoded RFC 3986 URI query style instead, see
305                 * {@link #encodedKeyValues()}.
306                 * @return formatter.
307                 */
308                public Builder keyValues() {
309                        return add(LogbackKeyValuesFormatter.INSTANCE);
310                }
311
312                /**
313                 * Creates a formatter that will print the key values in order of the passed in
314                 * keys if they exist, Logback <code>%X</code> style (see {@link #keyValues()} for
315                 * the exact format). <strong>An empty list is considered a noop and no keys will
316                 * be ommitted!</strong> If you want all keys use {@link #keyValues()}. For the
317                 * percent-encoded style instead, see {@link #encodedKeyValues(List)}.
318                 * @param keys keys where order is important.
319                 * @return this.
320                 */
321                public Builder keyValues(List<String> keys) {
322                        if (keys.isEmpty()) {
323                                return this;
324                        }
325                        return add(new LogbackListKeyValuesFormatter(keys));
326                }
327
328                /**
329                 * Creates a formatter that will print a single key's value, Logback/Log4j2
330                 * <code>%X{key}</code> style: just the raw value (or the fallback, or an empty
331                 * string if neither is present) - no key prefix, no percent encoding. For the
332                 * percent-encoded <code>key=value</code> style instead, see
333                 * {@link #encodedKeyValue(String, String)}.
334                 * @param key key to select.
335                 * @param fallback if the value is null the fallback will be used.
336                 * @return this.
337                 */
338                public Builder keyValue(String key, @Nullable String fallback) {
339                        return add(new LogbackSingleKeyValueFormatter(key, fallback));
340                }
341
342                /**
343                 * Creates a formatter that will print <strong>ALL</strong> of the key values by
344                 * percent encoding (RFC 3986 URI aka the format usually used in
345                 * {@link URI#getQuery()}). Keys that are mapped to <code>null</code> will only
346                 * have the key printed and no separating equal sign (<code>=</code>). This is to
347                 * differentiate empty string and <code>null</code> - the same behavior as
348                 * {@link KeyValueNullStrategy#KEEP}. For Logback's <code>%X</code> style instead,
349                 * see {@link #keyValues()}.
350                 * @return formatter.
351                 */
352                public Builder encodedKeyValues() {
353                        return add(DefaultKeyValuesFormatter.INSTANCE);
354                }
355
356                /**
357                 * Creates a formatter that will print the key values in order of the passed in
358                 * keys if they exist in percent encoding (RFC 3986 URI aka the format usually
359                 * used in {@link URI#getQuery()}), preserving the <code>null</code>/empty-string
360                 * distinction for a key whose value is <code>null</code>
361                 * ({@link KeyValueNullStrategy#KEEP} - most key values, e.g. MDC, are never
362                 * actually mapped to <code>null</code> in practice, so this only matters if yours
363                 * are). <strong>An empty {@code keys} list is a noop - no formatter is added at
364                 * all.</strong> If you want all keys use {@link #encodedKeyValues()}. For
365                 * Logback's <code>%X</code> style instead, see {@link #keyValues(List)}.
366                 * @param keys keys where order is important.
367                 * @return this.
368                 * @see #encodedKeyValues(List, KeyValueNullStrategy)
369                 */
370                public Builder encodedKeyValues(List<String> keys) {
371                        return encodedKeyValues(keys, KeyValueNullStrategy.KEEP);
372                }
373
374                /**
375                 * Creates a formatter that will print the key values in order of the passed in
376                 * keys if they exist in percent encoding (RFC 3986 URI aka the format usually
377                 * used in {@link URI#getQuery()}), handling keys whose value is <code>null</code>
378                 * (or simply absent - the two are indistinguishable, see
379                 * {@link KeyValueNullStrategy}) according to <code>nullStrategy</code>.
380                 * <strong>An empty {@code keys} list is a noop - no formatter is added at
381                 * all.</strong> If you want all keys use {@link #encodedKeyValues()}. For
382                 * Logback's <code>%X</code> style instead, see {@link #keyValues(List)}.
383                 * @param keys keys where order is important.
384                 * @param nullStrategy how to handle a key whose value is <code>null</code> or
385                 * absent.
386                 * @return this.
387                 */
388                public Builder encodedKeyValues(List<String> keys, KeyValueNullStrategy nullStrategy) {
389                        if (keys.isEmpty()) {
390                                return this;
391                        }
392                        return add(new SelectedEncodedKeyValuesFormatter(keys, nullStrategy));
393                }
394
395                /**
396                 * Creates a formatter that will print a single key value in percent encoding (RFC
397                 * 3986 URI aka the format usually used in {@link URI#getQuery()}). For Logback/
398                 * Log4j2's <code>%X{key}</code> style instead, see
399                 * {@link #keyValue(String, String)}.
400                 * @param key key to select.
401                 * @param fallback if the value is null the fallback will be used.
402                 * @return this.
403                 */
404                public Builder encodedKeyValue(String key, @Nullable String fallback) {
405                        return add(new SingleKeyValueFormatter(key, fallback));
406                }
407
408                /**
409                 * Appends a space.
410                 * @return this builder.
411                 */
412                public Builder space() {
413                        formatters.add(new StaticFormatter(" "));
414                        return this;
415                }
416
417                /**
418                 * Appends a newline using the platforms line separator.
419                 * @return this builder.
420                 */
421                public Builder newline() {
422                        text(System.lineSeparator());
423                        return this;
424                }
425
426                /**
427                 * Appends a thread name : {@link Thread#getName()}.
428                 * @return this builder.
429                 */
430                public Builder threadName() {
431                        formatters.add(DefaultThreadFormatter.THREAD_NAME_FORMATTER);
432                        return this;
433                }
434
435                /**
436                 * Appends a thread ID : {@link Thread#threadId()}.
437                 * @return this builder.
438                 */
439                public Builder threadId() {
440                        formatters.add(DefaultThreadFormatter.THREAD_ID_FORMATTER);
441                        return this;
442                }
443
444                /**
445                 * Appends the events throwable stack trace.
446                 * @return this.
447                 */
448                public Builder throwable() {
449                        formatters.add(ThrowableFormatter.of());
450                        return this;
451                }
452
453                /**
454                 * Appends the events throwable stack trace using a custom
455                 * {@link ThrowableFormatter} (e.g. one created with
456                 * {@link ThrowableFormatter#builder()}).
457                 * @param throwableFormatter formatter to use.
458                 * @return this.
459                 */
460                public Builder throwable(ThrowableFormatter throwableFormatter) {
461                        formatters.add(throwableFormatter);
462                        return this;
463                }
464
465                /**
466                 * Will create a generic log formatter that has the inner formatters coalesced if
467                 * possible and will noop if there are no formatters.
468                 * @return flattened formatter.
469                 */
470                public LogFormatter build() {
471                        var array = StaticFormatter.coalesce(formatters);
472                        if (array.length == 0) {
473                                return NoopFormatter.INSTANCE;
474                        }
475                        if (array.length == 1) {
476                                return array[0];
477                        }
478                        return EventFormatter.of(formatters);
479                }
480
481                /**
482                 * Creates the formatter and converts it to an encoder.
483                 * @return encoder.
484                 * @apiNote for ergonomics
485                 */
486                public LogEncoder encoder() {
487                        return LogEncoder.of(build());
488                }
489
490        }
491
492        /**
493         * Generic event formatting that is lambda friendly.
494         */
495        @FunctionalInterface
496        public non-sealed interface EventFormatter extends LogFormatter {
497
498                @Override
499                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event);
500
501                private static EventFormatter of(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
502                        return new CompositeFormatter(StaticFormatter.coalesce(formatters));
503                }
504
505        }
506
507        /**
508         * Formats a {@link Level}.
509         */
510        public sealed interface LevelFormatter extends LogFormatter {
511
512                /**
513                 * Formats the level.
514                 * @param output buffer.
515                 * @param level level.
516                 */
517                void formatLevel(StringBuilder output, Level level);
518
519                @Override
520                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
521                        formatLevel(output, event.level());
522                }
523
524                /**
525                 * Formats a level.
526                 * @param level level
527                 * @return formatted level as a string.
528                 */
529                default String formatLevel(Level level) {
530                        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
531                        formatLevel(sb, level);
532                        return sb.toString();
533                }
534
535                /**
536                 * Default implementation calls {@link LevelFormatter#toString(Level)}
537                 * @return formatter.
538                 */
539                public static LevelFormatter of() {
540                        return DefaultLevelFormatter.LEVEL_FORMATTER;
541                }
542
543                /**
544                 * Default implementation calls {@link LevelFormatter#rightPadded(Level)}
545                 * @return formatter.
546                 */
547                public static LevelFormatter ofRightPadded() {
548                        return DefaultLevelFormatter.RIGHT_PAD_LEVEL_FORMATTER;
549                }
550
551                /**
552                 * Turns a Level into a SLF4J like level String that is all upper case.
553                 * {@link Level#ALL} is "<code>TRACE</code>", {@link Level#OFF} is
554                 * "<code>ERROR</code>" and {@link Level#WARNING} is "<code>WARN</code>".
555                 * @param level system logger level.
556                 * @return upper case string of level.
557                 */
558                public static String toString(Level level) {
559                        return switch (level) {
560                                case DEBUG -> "DEBUG";
561                                case ALL -> "TRACE";
562                                case ERROR -> "ERROR";
563                                case INFO -> "INFO";
564                                case OFF -> "ERROR";
565                                case TRACE -> "TRACE";
566                                case WARNING -> "WARN";
567                        };
568                }
569
570                /**
571                 * Turns a Level into a SLF4J like level String that is all upper case and same
572                 * length with right padding. {@link Level#ALL} is "<code>TRACE</code>",
573                 * {@link Level#OFF} is "<code>ERROR</code>" and {@link Level#WARNING} is
574                 * "<code>WARN</code>".
575                 * @param level system logger level.
576                 * @return upper case string of level.
577                 */
578                public static String rightPadded(Level level) {
579                        return switch (level) {
580                                case DEBUG -> /*   */ "DEBUG";
581                                case ALL -> /*     */ "TRACE";
582                                case ERROR -> /*   */ "ERROR";
583                                case INFO -> /*    */ "INFO ";
584                                case OFF -> /*     */ "ERROR";
585                                case TRACE -> /*   */ "TRACE";
586                                case WARNING -> /* */ "WARN ";
587                        };
588                }
589
590        }
591
592        /**
593         * Formats event timestamps.
594         */
595        public sealed interface TimestampFormatter extends LogFormatter {
596
597                /**
598                 * The default timestamp format used in many logging frameworks which does not
599                 * have dates and only time at millisecond precision.
600                 * <p>
601                 * It is called TTLL as that is the name of the format where it is used in
602                 * logback, log4j etc.
603                 */
604                public static String TTLL_TIME_FORMAT = "HH:mm:ss.SSS";
605
606                /**
607                 * Format timestamp.
608                 * @param output buffer.
609                 * @param instant timestamp.
610                 */
611                void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant);
612
613                @Override
614                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
615                        formatTimestamp(output, event.timestamp());
616                }
617
618                /**
619                 * Formats timestamp using {@link #TTLL_TIME_FORMAT}.
620                 * @return formatter.
621                 */
622                public static TimestampFormatter of() {
623                        return DefaultInstantFormatter.TTLL;
624                }
625
626                /**
627                 * Formats a timestamp using ISO format at fixed millisecond precision (e.g.
628                 * {@code 2023-11-14T22:13:20.123Z}, always exactly 3 fractional digits). Pair
629                 * with {@link #ofMicros()} to append additional sub-millisecond digits, similar
630                 * to Logback's {@code %d{ISO8601}%microsecond}.
631                 * @return formatter.
632                 */
633                public static TimestampFormatter ofISO() {
634                        return DefaultInstantFormatter.ISO;
635                }
636
637                /**
638                 * Micro seconds over the events last second. This is for logback compatibility.
639                 * @return microseconds zero padded.
640                 */
641                public static TimestampFormatter ofMicros() {
642                        return MicrosInstantFormatter.INSTANCE;
643                }
644
645                /**
646                 * Formats a timestamp using standard JDK date time formatter.
647                 * @param dateTimeFormatter date time formatter.
648                 * @return timestamp formatter.
649                 */
650                public static TimestampFormatter of(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter) {
651                        return of(dateTimeFormatter, false);
652                }
653
654                /**
655                 * Formats a timestamp using standard JDK date time formatter.
656                 * <p>
657                 * Formatting with {@link DateTimeFormatter} is comparatively expensive to do on
658                 * every event, so if the caller knows the formatter's finest resolution is
659                 * milliseconds (e.g. a pattern using at most {@code SSS}, never
660                 * {@code n}/{@code N} nanosecond fields), {@code cacheMillisecondPrecision} can
661                 * be set to {@code true} to reuse the previously formatted string whenever
662                 * consecutive events land in the same millisecond - the same trick Logback's
663                 * {@code CachingDateFormatter} and Log4j2's {@code FixedDateFormat} use. Passing
664                 * {@code true} for a formatter that can actually render sub-millisecond precision
665                 * will silently truncate that precision, so only pass {@code true} when the
666                 * pattern is known to not exceed millisecond resolution.
667                 * @param dateTimeFormatter date time formatter.
668                 * @param cacheMillisecondPrecision {@code true} if the formatter's output is
669                 * fully determined by the instant's millisecond value.
670                 * @return timestamp formatter.
671                 */
672                public static TimestampFormatter of(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter, boolean cacheMillisecondPrecision) {
673                        return new DateTimeFormatterInstantFormatter(dateTimeFormatter, cacheMillisecondPrecision);
674                }
675
676        }
677
678        /**
679         * Formats a throwable.
680         */
681        public non-sealed interface ThrowableFormatter extends LogFormatter {
682
683                /**
684                 * Formats a throwable and appends.
685                 * @param output buffer.
686                 * @param throwable throwable.
687                 */
688                void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable);
689
690                @Override
691                default void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
692                        var t = event.throwableOrNull();
693                        if (t != null) {
694                                formatThrowable(output, t);
695                        }
696                }
697
698                /**
699                 * Default implementation uses {@link Throwable#printStackTrace(PrintWriter)}.
700                 * This formatter is equivalent to {@code of(Integer.MAX_VALUE, List.of())} except
701                 * that it defers entirely to {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} and thus will
702                 * respect any override of that method a particular {@link Throwable} subclass
703                 * might have.
704                 * @return formatter.
705                 */
706                public static ThrowableFormatter of() {
707                        return DefaultThrowableFormatter.INSTANT;
708                }
709
710                /**
711                 * Creates a builder for a throwable formatter that can limit the number of stack
712                 * frame lines shown for each throwable in the cause/suppressed chain, exclude
713                 * frames matching regular expressions, and append packaging data. The output is
714                 * otherwise formatted like {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()}: common frames
715                 * shared with the enclosing throwable are elided the same way (e.g.
716                 * <code>"... 6 more"</code>) as long as the depth limit was not what stopped
717                 * printing; if the depth limit is what stopped printing a
718                 * <code>"... N frames truncated"</code> line is emitted instead.
719                 * @return builder.
720                 * @apiNote a builder left at its defaults (no max lines, exclusions, or packaging
721                 * data) builds {@link #of()} itself; otherwise the built formatter walks
722                 * {@link Throwable#getCause()}/{@link Throwable#getSuppressed()}/
723                 * {@link Throwable#getStackTrace()} directly instead of calling
724                 * {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} and thus will not honor a custom override
725                 * of that method.
726                 */
727                public static Builder builder() {
728                        return new Builder();
729                }
730
731                /**
732                 * Convenience to append a throwable to string builder.
733                 * @param b buffer.
734                 * @param t throwable.
735                 * @apiNote this call creates garbage.
736                 */
737                public static void appendThrowable(StringBuilder b, Throwable t) {
738                        /*
739                         * TODO optimize
740                         */
741                        t.printStackTrace(Internal.StringBuilderPrintWriter.of(b));
742                }
743
744                /**
745                 * Builds a configurable {@link ThrowableFormatter}.
746                 *
747                 * @see ThrowableFormatter#builder()
748                 */
749                public final class Builder {
750
751                        private int maxLines = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
752
753                        private List<String> excludes = List.of();
754
755                        private boolean packagingData = false;
756
757                        private Builder() {
758                        }
759
760                        /**
761                         * Maximum number of stack frame ("at ...") lines printed per throwable in the
762                         * chain. Use {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} for no limit (the default, and matches
763                         * {@link ThrowableFormatter#of()} for well behaved throwables). {@code 0}
764                         * prints just the throwable header lines (class and message) for the whole
765                         * chain with no frames at all.
766                         * @param maxLines maximum stack frame lines per throwable.
767                         * @return this builder.
768                         */
769                        public Builder maxLines(int maxLines) {
770                                this.maxLines = maxLines;
771                                return this;
772                        }
773
774                        /**
775                         * Regular expressions matched with {@link Matcher#find()} against each
776                         * frame's {@link StackTraceElement#toString()}. A frame matching any of these
777                         * is omitted entirely and does not count against {@link #maxLines(int)}.
778                         * Defaults to empty (no filtering).
779                         * @param excludes exclude patterns.
780                         * @return this builder.
781                         */
782                        public Builder excludes(List<String> excludes) {
783                                this.excludes = excludes;
784                                return this;
785                        }
786
787                        /**
788                         * Whether to append packaging data (the jar or module a frame's class was
789                         * loaded from, and its version) after each frame line, e.g.
790                         * <code>[myapp-1.0.jar:1.0]</code> or <code>[java.base:na]</code>. This
791                         * mirrors (but does not byte-for-byte match) logback's
792                         * <code>ExtendedThrowableProxyConverter</code> output. Resolution requires
793                         * loading the frame's class (without initializing it) and can fail silently
794                         * to <code>[na:na]</code> for frames whose class cannot be loaded (e.g.
795                         * dynamically generated classes). This has a real per-frame cost so it
796                         * defaults to <code>false</code>.
797                         * @param packagingData true to append packaging data.
798                         * @return this builder.
799                         */
800                        public Builder packagingData(boolean packagingData) {
801                                this.packagingData = packagingData;
802                                return this;
803                        }
804
805                        /**
806                         * Builds the formatter. If none of {@link #maxLines(int)},
807                         * {@link #excludes(List)}, or {@link #packagingData(boolean)} were set away
808                         * from their defaults, returns {@link ThrowableFormatter#of()} (i.e. plain
809                         * {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()} behavior) instead of constructing a
810                         * formatter that walks the throwable manually for no reason.
811                         * @return formatter.
812                         */
813                        public ThrowableFormatter build() {
814                                if (maxLines == Integer.MAX_VALUE && excludes.isEmpty() && !packagingData) {
815                                        return ThrowableFormatter.of();
816                                }
817                                List<Pattern> compiled = excludes.isEmpty() ? List.of()
818                                                : excludes.stream().map(Pattern::compile).toList();
819                                var resolver = packagingData ? new PackagingDataResolver() : null;
820                                return new StandardThrowableFormatter(maxLines, compiled, resolver);
821                        }
822
823                }
824
825        }
826
827        /**
828         * Tests if the log formatter is noop or is null which will be considered as noop.
829         * @param logFormatter formatter which <strong>can be <code>null</code></strong>!
830         * @return true if the formatter should not be used.
831         */
832        public static boolean isNoopOrNull(@Nullable LogFormatter logFormatter) {
833                return logFormatter == null || logFormatter.isNoop();
834        }
835
836        /**
837         * Pads the right hand side of text with space.
838         * @param sb buffer.
839         * @param s string that will be appended first (left hand) and will not be longer than
840         * the <code>n</code> parameter.
841         * @param n the size of string. If the size is bigger than passed in string the result
842         * will have padding otherwise the passed in string will be cut to the size of this
843         * parameter.
844         */
845        public static void padRight(StringBuilder sb, CharSequence s, int n) {
846                int length = s.length();
847                if (length >= n) {
848                        sb.append(s, 0, n);
849                        return;
850                }
851                sb.append(s);
852                spacePad(sb, n - length);
853        }
854
855        /**
856         * Pads the left hand side of text with space.
857         * @param sb buffer.
858         * @param s string that will be appended second (right hand) and will not be longer
859         * than the <code>n</code> parameter.
860         * @param n the size of string. If the size is bigger than passed in string the result
861         * will have padding otherwise the passed in string will be cut to the size of this
862         * parameter.
863         */
864        public static void padLeft(StringBuilder sb, CharSequence s, int n) {
865                int length = s.length();
866                if (length >= n) {
867                        sb.append(s, 0, n);
868                        return;
869                }
870                spacePad(sb, n - length);
871                sb.append(s);
872        }
873
874        /**
875         * Fast space padding method.
876         */
877        private static void spacePad(final StringBuilder sbuf, final int length) {
878                int l = length;
879                while (l >= 32) {
880                        sbuf.append(CompositeFormatter.SPACES[5]);
881                        l -= 32;
882                }
883
884                for (int i = 4; i >= 0; i--) {
885                        if ((l & (1 << i)) != 0) {
886                                sbuf.append(CompositeFormatter.SPACES[i]);
887                        }
888                }
889        }
890
891        /**
892         * A special formatter that will do nothing.
893         */
894        enum NoopFormatter implements TimestampFormatter, ThrowableFormatter, LevelFormatter {
895
896                /**
897                 * instance.
898                 */
899                INSTANCE;
900
901                @Override
902                public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
903                }
904
905                @Override
906                public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
907                }
908
909                @Override
910                public void formatLevel(StringBuilder output, Level level) {
911                }
912
913                @Override
914                public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
915                }
916
917        }
918
919}

921@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent")
922record CompositeFormatter(LogFormatter[] formatters) implements EventFormatter {
923
924        static String[] SPACES = { " ", "  ", "    ", "        ", // 1,2,4,8 spaces
925                        "                ", // 16 spaces
926                        "                                " }; // 32 spaces
927
928        @Override
929        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
930                for (var formatter : formatters) {
931                        formatter.format(output, event);
932                }
933        }
934
935        @Override
936        public String toString() {
937                return getClass().getSimpleName() + Arrays.toString(formatters);
938        }
939
940        public static List<LogFormatter> flatten(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
941                return List.copyOf(_flatten(formatters));
942        }
943
944        private static List<LogFormatter> _flatten(List<? extends LogFormatter> formatters) {
945                List<LogFormatter> result = new ArrayList<>();
946                for (var f : formatters) {
947                        if (f instanceof CompositeFormatter cf) {
948                                result.addAll(_flatten(cf));
949                        }
950                        else {
951                                result.add(f);
952                        }
953                }
954                return result;
955        }
956
957        private static List<LogFormatter> _flatten(CompositeFormatter formatter) {
958                var formatters = formatter.formatters;
959                return _flatten(Arrays.asList(formatters));
960        }
961
962}

1022/**
1023 * Not an enum: error-prone's immutable-enum check flags enums holding mutable state, and
1024 * {@link #cache} is mutable (an {@link java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference}).
1025 * {@link #description} exists solely to give each instance a stable identity for
1026 * {@link #toString()}.
1027 */
1028final class DefaultInstantFormatter implements TimestampFormatter {
1029
1030        static final DefaultInstantFormatter TTLL = new DefaultInstantFormatter("TTLL",
1031                        DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(TTLL_TIME_FORMAT).withZone(ZoneId.from(ZoneOffset.UTC)));
1032
1033        /*
1034         * appendInstant(3) renders a fixed-width 3-digit millisecond fraction (unlike
1035         * DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME, which renders a variable-width fraction of 0-9
1036         * digits based on the instant's actual sub-millisecond value) - fixed width matches
1037         * Logback/Log4j2's ISO output and is what makes this safe to millis-cache.
1038         */
1039        static final DefaultInstantFormatter ISO = new DefaultInstantFormatter("ISO",
1040                        new DateTimeFormatterBuilder().appendInstant(3).toFormatter());
1041
1042        private final String description;
1043
1044        private final DateTimeFormatter formatter;
1045
1046        private final MillisCache cache = new MillisCache();
1047
1048        private DefaultInstantFormatter(String description, DateTimeFormatter formatter) {
1049                this.description = description;
1050                this.formatter = formatter;
1051        }
1052
1053        @Override
1054        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {

1056        }

1058        @Override

1065/**
1066 * Micro seconds over the events last second, for Logback compatibility - meant to be
1067 * composed after a millisecond-precision timestamp (see
1068 * {@link TimestampFormatter#ofISO()}). Stateless, so a singleton enum works cleanly here
1069 * (unlike {@link DefaultInstantFormatter}, nothing here trips error-prone's
1070 * immutable-enum check).
1071 */
1072enum MicrosInstantFormatter implements TimestampFormatter {
1073
1074        INSTANCE;
1075
1076        @Override
1077        @SuppressWarnings("JavaInstantGetSecondsGetNano")
1078        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
1079                int nanos = instant.getNano();
1080
1081                int millis_and_micros = nanos / 1000;
1082                int micros = millis_and_micros % 1000;
1083
1084                if (micros >= 100) {
1085                        output.append(micros);
1086                }
1087                else if (micros >= 10) {
1088                        output.append("0").append(micros);
1089                }
1090                else {
1091                        output.append("00").append(micros);
1092                }
1093        }
1094
1095}

1103        DateTimeFormatterInstantFormatter(DateTimeFormatter dateTimeFormatter, boolean cacheMillisecondPrecision) {

1106        }

1109        public void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant) {
1110                var c = cache;
1111                if (c == null) {
1112                        dateTimeFormatter.formatTo(instant, output);

1120/**
1121 * Caches a formatted timestamp string keyed by the instant's millisecond value, the same
1122 * trick Logback's {@code CachingDateFormatter} and Log4j2's {@code FixedDateFormat} use -
1123 * reformatting only happens when consecutive events land in different milliseconds. Only
1124 * correct for formatters whose output is fully determined by millisecond precision
1125 * (callers are responsible for that guarantee).
1126 */
1127final class MillisCache {
1128
1129        private record Entry(long millis, String formatted) {
1130        }
1131
1132        private static final Entry EMPTY = new Entry(Long.MIN_VALUE, "");
1133
1134        private final AtomicReference<Entry> ref = new AtomicReference<>(EMPTY);
1135
1136        void formatTimestamp(StringBuilder output, Instant instant, DateTimeFormatter formatter) {
1137                long millis = instant.toEpochMilli();
1138                Entry cached = ref.get();
1139                if (cached.millis() == millis) {
1140                        output.append(cached.formatted());
1141                        return;
1142                }
1143                StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(32);
1144                formatter.formatTo(instant, sb);
1145                String formatted = sb.toString();
1146                ref.set(new Entry(millis, formatted));
1147                output.append(formatted);
1148        }
1149
1150}

1163/**
1164 * Reimplements {@link Throwable#printStackTrace()}'s algorithm (header line, frames,
1165 * common-frame elision against the enclosing trace, "Caused by:"/"Suppressed:" sections,
1166 * circular reference guard) so that a max line count and frame exclusion patterns can be
1167 * applied while printing.
1168 */
1169final class StandardThrowableFormatter implements ThrowableFormatter {
1170
1171        private static final String CAUSE_CAPTION = "Caused by: ";
1172
1173        private static final String SUPPRESSED_CAPTION = "Suppressed: ";
1174
1175        private final int maxLines;
1176
1177        private final List<Pattern> excludes;
1178
1179        private final @Nullable PackagingDataResolver packagingData;
1180
1181        StandardThrowableFormatter(int maxLines, List<Pattern> excludes, @Nullable PackagingDataResolver packagingData) {
1182                this.maxLines = maxLines;
1183                this.excludes = excludes;
1184                this.packagingData = packagingData;
1185        }
1186
1187        @Override
1188        public void formatThrowable(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable) {
1189                Set<Throwable> dejaVu = Collections.newSetFromMap(new IdentityHashMap<>());
1190                dejaVu.add(throwable);
1191                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1192                output.append(throwable).append(System.lineSeparator());
1193                printFrames(output, trace, trace.length, "");
1194                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1195                        printEnclosed(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, "\t", dejaVu);
1196                }
1197                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1198                if (cause != null) {
1199                        printEnclosed(output, cause, trace, CAUSE_CAPTION, "", dejaVu);
1200                }
1201        }
1202
1203        private void printEnclosed(StringBuilder output, Throwable throwable, StackTraceElement[] enclosingTrace,
1204                        String caption, String prefix, Set<Throwable> dejaVu) {
1205                if (!dejaVu.add(throwable)) {
1206                        output.append(prefix)
1207                                .append("[CIRCULAR REFERENCE: ")
1208                                .append(throwable)
1209                                .append(']')
1210                                .append(System.lineSeparator());
1211                        return;
1212                }
1213                var trace = throwable.getStackTrace();
1214                int m = trace.length - 1;
1215                int n = enclosingTrace.length - 1;
1216                while (m >= 0 && n >= 0 && trace[m].equals(enclosingTrace[n])) {
1217                        m--;
1218                        n--;
1219                }
1220                int framesInCommon = trace.length - 1 - m;
1221                output.append(prefix).append(caption).append(throwable).append(System.lineSeparator());
1222                boolean truncated = printFrames(output, trace, m + 1, prefix);
1223                if (!truncated && framesInCommon > 0) {
1224                        output.append(prefix)
1225                                .append("\t... ")
1226                                .append(framesInCommon)
1227                                .append(" more")
1228                                .append(System.lineSeparator());
1229                }
1230                for (var suppressed : throwable.getSuppressed()) {
1231                        printEnclosed(output, suppressed, trace, SUPPRESSED_CAPTION, prefix + "\t", dejaVu);
1232                }
1233                var cause = throwable.getCause();
1234                if (cause != null) {
1235                        printEnclosed(output, cause, trace, CAUSE_CAPTION, prefix, dejaVu);
1236                }
1237        }
1238
1239        /*
1240         * Prints frames trace[0..count) filtered by excludes and capped at maxLines. Returns
1241         * true if there were excluded-filtered frames beyond maxLines (i.e. the output was
1242         * cut short because of maxLines rather than ending naturally).
1243         */
1244        private boolean printFrames(StringBuilder output, StackTraceElement[] trace, int count, String prefix) {
1245                int printed = 0;
1246                int available = 0;
1247                for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
1248                        var element = trace[i];
1249                        if (isExcluded(element)) {
1250                                continue;
1251                        }
1252                        available++;
1253                        if (printed < maxLines) {
1254                                output.append(prefix).append("\tat ").append(element);
1255                                // Eclipse null analysis is too dumb about final fields.
1256                                var packagingData = this.packagingData;
1257                                if (packagingData != null) {
1258                                        output.append(' ').append(packagingData.resolve(element));
1259                                }
1260                                output.append(System.lineSeparator());
1261                                printed++;
1262                        }
1263                }
1264                if (available > maxLines) {
1265                        output.append(prefix)
1266                                .append("\t... ")
1267                                .append(available - maxLines)
1268                                .append(" frames truncated")
1269                                .append(System.lineSeparator());
1270                        return true;
1271                }
1272                return false;
1273        }
1274
1275        private boolean isExcluded(StackTraceElement element) {
1276                if (excludes.isEmpty()) {
1277                        return false;
1278                }
1279                String s = element.toString();
1280                for (var p : excludes) {
1281                        Matcher matcher = p.matcher(s);
1282                        if (matcher.find()) {
1283                                return true;
1284                        }
1285                }
1286                return false;
1287        }
1288
1289}
1290
1291/**
1292 * Resolves and caches which jar/module/directory a stack frame's class was loaded from
1293 * and its reported version, formatted as <code>[location:version]</code>. Named modules
1294 * (including JDK frames) are resolved for free from the frame itself or the loaded
1295 * class's {@link Module} without touching a {@link java.security.CodeSource}. Classpath
1296 * (unnamed module) frames fall back to the class's {@link java.security.CodeSource} and
1297 * {@link Package#getImplementationVersion()}. Either "location" or "version" is
1298 * <code>na</code> when unknown, and the whole result is <code>[na:na]</code> when the
1299 * frame's class cannot be loaded at all (e.g. dynamically generated classes).
1300 */
1301final class PackagingDataResolver {
1302
1303        private final ConcurrentMap<String, String> cache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
1304
1305        String resolve(StackTraceElement element) {
1306                String className = element.getClassName();
1307                String cached = cache.get(className);
1308                if (cached != null) {
1309                        return cached;
1310                }
1311                String computed = compute(element);
1312                cache.put(className, computed);
1313                return computed;
1314        }
1315
1316        private static String compute(StackTraceElement element) {
1317                String moduleName = element.getModuleName();
1318                if (moduleName != null) {
1319                        return format(moduleName, element.getModuleVersion());
1320                }
1321                Class<?> type = load(element.getClassName());
1322                if (type == null) {
1323                        return "[na:na]";
1324                }
1325                Module module = type.getModule();
1326                if (module.isNamed()) {
1327                        var descriptor = module.getDescriptor();
1328                        String version = descriptor == null ? null : descriptor.rawVersion().orElse(null);
1329                        return format(module.getName(), version);
1330                }
1331                var codeSource = type.getProtectionDomain().getCodeSource();
1332                if (codeSource == null) {
1333                        return "[na:na]";
1334                }
1335                var location = codeSource.getLocation();
1336                if (location == null) {
1337                        return "[na:na]";
1338                }
1339                String path = location.getPath();
1340                if (path == null || path.isEmpty()) {
1341                        path = location.toString();
1342                }
1343                if (path.endsWith("/")) {
1344                        path = path.substring(0, path.length() - 1);
1345                }
1346                int slash = path.lastIndexOf('/');
1347                String name = slash >= 0 && slash < path.length() - 1 ? path.substring(slash + 1) : path;
1348                var pkg = type.getPackage();
1349                String version = pkg == null ? null : pkg.getImplementationVersion();
1350                return format(name, version);
1351        }
1352
1353        private static String format(String location, @Nullable String version) {
1354                return "[" + location + ":" + (version == null || version.isEmpty() ? "na" : version) + "]";
1355        }
1356
1357        private static @Nullable Class<?> load(String className) {
1358                var contextLoader = Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader();
1359                if (contextLoader != null) {
1360                        var type = loadOrNull(className, contextLoader);
1361                        if (type != null) {
1362                                return type;
1363                        }
1364                }
1365                return loadOrNull(className, PackagingDataResolver.class.getClassLoader());
1366        }
1367
1368        private static @Nullable Class<?> loadOrNull(String className, @Nullable ClassLoader loader) {
1369                try {
1370                        return Class.forName(className, false, loader);
1371                }
1372                catch (ClassNotFoundException | LinkageError | SecurityException e) {
1373                        return null;
1374                }
1375        }
1376
1377}

1408final class SelectedEncodedKeyValuesFormatter implements LogFormatter {
1409
1410        private final String[] keys;
1411
1412        private final KeyValueNullStrategy nullStrategy;
1413
1414        @SuppressWarnings("nullness")
1415        SelectedEncodedKeyValuesFormatter(List<String> keys, KeyValueNullStrategy nullStrategy) {
1416                var ks = List.copyOf(keys);
1417                this.keys = ks.toArray(new String[] {});
1418                this.nullStrategy = nullStrategy;
1419        }
1420
1421        @Override
1422        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1423                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1424                formatKeyValues(output, kvs);
1425        }
1426
1427        void formatKeyValues(StringBuilder output, KeyValues keyValues) {
1428                boolean first = true;
1429                for (String k : keys) {
1430                        @Nullable
1431                        String v = keyValues.getValueOrNull(k);
1432                        if (v == null) {
1433                                switch (nullStrategy) {
1434                                        case SKIP -> {
1435                                                continue;
1436                                        }
1437                                        case EMPTY -> v = "";
1438                                        case KEEP -> {
1439                                                /* leave v null - formatKeyValue will print the key only. */
1440                                        }
1441                                }
1442                        }
1443                        if (first) {
1444                                first = false;
1445                        }
1446                        else {
1447                                output.append("&");
1448                        }
1449                        DefaultKeyValuesFormatter.formatKeyValue(output, k, v);
1450                }
1451        }
1452
1453}
1454
1455record SingleKeyValueFormatter(String key, @Nullable String fallback) implements LogFormatter {
1456        @Override
1457        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1458                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1459                formatKeyValues(output, kvs);
1460        }
1461
1462        void formatKeyValues(StringBuilder output, KeyValues keyValues) {
1463                String v = keyValues.getValueOrNull(key);
1464                if (v == null) {
1465                        v = fallback;
1466                }
1467                DefaultKeyValuesFormatter.formatKeyValue(output, key, v);
1468        }
1469
1470}
1471
1472/**
1473 * Logback <code>%X</code> style: comma-space separated <code>key=value</code> pairs, no
1474 * surrounding braces, no percent encoding. See {@link LogFormatter.Builder#keyValues()}.
1475 */
1476enum LogbackKeyValuesFormatter implements LogFormatter, KeyValuesConsumer<StringBuilder> {
1477
1478        INSTANCE;
1479
1480        @Override
1481        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1482                var keyValues = event.keyValues();
1483                keyValues.forEach(this, 0, output);
1484        }
1485
1486        static void formatKeyValue(StringBuilder output, String k, @Nullable String v) {
1487                output.append(k);
1488                if (v != null) {
1489                        output.append("=").append(v);
1490                }
1491        }
1492
1493        @Override
1494        public int accept(KeyValues values, String key, @Nullable String value, int index, StringBuilder storage) {
1495                if (index > 0) {
1496                        storage.append(", ");
1497                }
1498                formatKeyValue(storage, key, value);
1499                return index + 1;
1500        }
1501
1502}
1503
1504final class LogbackListKeyValuesFormatter implements LogFormatter {
1505
1506        private final String[] keys;
1507
1508        @SuppressWarnings("nullness")
1509        LogbackListKeyValuesFormatter(List<String> keys) {
1510                var ks = List.copyOf(keys);
1511                this.keys = ks.toArray(new String[] {});
1512        }
1513
1514        @Override
1515        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1516                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1517                formatKeyValues(output, kvs);
1518        }
1519
1520        void formatKeyValues(StringBuilder output, KeyValues keyValues) {
1521                boolean first = true;
1522                for (String k : keys) {
1523                        String v = keyValues.getValueOrNull(k);
1524                        if (v == null) {
1525                                continue;
1526                        }
1527                        if (first) {
1528                                first = false;
1529                        }
1530                        else {
1531                                output.append(", ");
1532                        }
1533                        LogbackKeyValuesFormatter.formatKeyValue(output, k, v);
1534                }
1535        }
1536
1537}
1538
1539/**
1540 * Logback/Log4j2 <code>%X{key}</code> style: just the raw value (or fallback, or empty
1541 * string), no key prefix, no percent encoding. See
1542 * {@link LogFormatter.Builder#keyValue(String, String)}.
1543 */
1544record LogbackSingleKeyValueFormatter(String key, @Nullable String fallback) implements LogFormatter {
1545
1546        @Override
1547        public void format(StringBuilder output, LogEvent event) {
1548                var kvs = event.keyValues();
1549                String v = kvs.getValueOrNull(key);
1550                if (v == null) {
1551                        v = fallback;
1552                }
1553                if (v != null) {
1554                        output.append(v);
1555                }
1556        }
1557
1558}
